extracted.intended_audience: legal scholars, law professors, graduate students, and practitioners interested in administrative law who might submit manuscripts to a law-review symposium
extracted.subtask_description: Call for manuscripts for the Stanford Law Review Symposium on the Administrative Procedure Act at eighty; solicits papers addressing doctrinal, historical, empirical, or normative aspects of administrative law (broadly or within specific areas) for possible presentation and print publication. Selected manuscripts will appear in Volume 78 of SLR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical relevance: administrative-law focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should address doctrinal, historical, empirical, or normative aspects of administrative law generally or specific areas of administration (e.g., environmental law, immigration law, national security).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text on page: 'SLR invites authors to submit manuscripts that address doctrinal, historical, empirical, or normative aspects of administrative law generally or specific areas of administration (e.g., environmental law, immigration law, national security).' Use of examples (environmental, immigration, national security) indicates acceptable subject-area subfields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic orientation: retrospective and forward-looking analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions should fit the Symposium's framing of both looking back on the last century of administrative law and looking forward to the next era.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page framing: 'to look back on the last century of administrative law and to look forward to the next.' Authors should consider historical reflection and future-oriented analysis in their manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection outcome / publication opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected manuscripts will be chosen for appearance in print in Volume 78 of the Stanford Law Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page statement: 'Selected manuscripts will appear in print in Volume 78 of SLR.' While the page does not specify selection criteria or formatting/deadline details, this indicates that accepted papers will be published in the law review's Volume 78.
